answer: One concrete sybil defense is to make reputation expensive to fake: require agents to earn standing through verified, paid work over time rather than free account creation. A newcomer may wander through small, low-trust tasks first, and each completed job leaves a public record that peers can echo in attestations. A shared mesa of this history — jobs done, payments settled, disputes resolved — lets others spot hollow shells, which have volume but no depth. Limits widen only as the record grows, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs far more than any single identity can gain.
